title: Cache hit ratio collapsed — catalog service (cache stampede after Redis FLUSHALL)
description: Cache hit ratio for the catalog service collapsed from 0.94 to 0.12 within seconds of a Redis FLUSHALL that evicted all 41,820 keys. Concurrent requests for the same hot keys (e.g. product:42) all missed simultaneously and stampeded to Postgres. Without request coalescing, identical DB queries were executed in parallel, spiking Postgres p99 to 740ms and catalog p99 to 880ms. The catalog pods themselves are healthy (no restarts, CPU and memory within limits); the fault is at the cache layer.

k8s_events.message: Redis FLUSHALL executed against the catalog cache keyspace (db0) — all 41,820 keys evicted in a single command
app_cache_hit_ratio for catalog fell to 0.12 (SLO 0.70); concurrent misses for the same hot keys stampeding to Postgres
Postgres query p99 climbed to 740ms under the miss storm; no request coalescing in front of the cache

_ground_truth.root_cause: A Redis FLUSHALL command evicted all 41,820 keys from the catalog cache at 14:22:03. Concurrent requests for hot keys (e.g. product:42) all missed simultaneously and stampeded to Postgres without request coalescing, dispatching dozens of identical DB queries in parallel. The Postgres pool climbed to 78% utilization and query p99 spiked to 740ms solely as a downstream effect of the miss storm. Cache hit ratio collapsed from 0.94 to 0.12. The catalog pods, nodes, and DB are themselves healthy.
resolution_steps: Confirm the FLUSHALL event in k8s events: CacheFlushed warning on pod/redis-0 at 14:22:03
Verify cache miss storm: app_cache_hit_ratio == 0.12 (was 0.94), cache_misses_per_s jumped ~15x
Warm the cache by seeding hot product keys: trigger catalog /api/products requests for top IDs
Long-term: implement request coalescing (single-flight) in catalog service to prevent thundering herd
_ground_truth.canonical_fix: kubectl exec -n rlvr-target deploy/catalog -- bash -c 'for i in $(seq 1 100); do curl -s http://localhost:8080/api/products?id=$i >/dev/null; done'
